summary.text: The United Nations is an international organization established by the Charter signed on 26 June 1945 to maintain peace and security and to promote cooperation among states.
With 193 member states it is the largest international organization in the world, and its headquarters is in New York City.
It has primarily focused on economic and social development, particularly during the wave of decolonization in the mid-twentieth century.

facts.label: Member states
facts.value: 193, the largest international organization in the world

facts.label: Principal organizations
facts.value: Six, including the General Assembly and Security Council

facts.label: Observer states
facts.value: The Holy See and the State of Palestine

items.prompt: The League of Nations needed unanimity for its substantive decisions. What was the stated reason for that rule?

options.label: To give the United States a veto
To speed up the League's decisions
To keep Germany off the Council
To uphold national sovereignty

items.explain: The unanimity requirement was negotiated in the name of upholding national sovereignty.

items.prompt: Ethiopia's emperor begged the League at Geneva for help against invasion. What came of it?

options.label: No intervention came, and calls for economic sanctions failed
The League sent troops and sanctions were imposed
The League expelled the invading country at once
The United States stepped in on the League's behalf

items.explain: The emperor's 1936 appeal went to no avail, and calls for economic sanctions against Italy failed.

items.prompt: In October 1943 four Allied powers signed a declaration on general security. What was it the first public sign of?

options.label: A plan to merge the League and the Red Cross
The signing of the UN Charter itself
A new body planned to replace the League
A peace deal ending the war

items.explain: The Four Power Declaration was the first public announcement that a new international organization was being considered to replace the League of Nations.

items.prompt: In 1942, during the war, what did a country have to do to join the Allies under the name United Nations?

options.label: Pay dues to a world court at Geneva
Sign the Declaration and declare war on the Axis powers
Send troops to the armies fighting in Europe
Join the League of Nations first

items.explain: Countries joined by signing the Declaration and declaring war on the Axis powers.

items.prompt: Compared with the Atlantic Charter, what major change did the Declaration by the United Nations make?

options.label: It gave France a leading role
It dropped Soviet suggestions
It added a provision for religious freedom
It removed the goals for the post-war world

items.explain: The major change was a provision for religious freedom, which Stalin approved after Roosevelt insisted; the text included Soviet suggestions but no role for France.

items.prompt: Delegations from the Allied Big Four negotiated the new organization's aims, structure and functioning at which conference?

options.label: The Tehran Conference
The Paris Peace Conference
The Arcadia Conference
The Dumbarton Oaks Conference

items.explain: The new organization was formulated and negotiated at Dumbarton Oaks; Tehran only discussed the idea, and some issues were resolved later at Yalta.
